A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CLIP-SVD work despite the changed title. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original few-shot classification, generalization, segmentation, efficiency, and ablation results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds comparator results, semantic-relevance ratings, corpus statistics, and SVD preprocessing measurements.

M1.justification: Both versions tune singular values while freezing singular vectors in both encoders' attention and MLP weights, using the same TextSpan interpretation procedure. v3 clarifies reconstruction, caching, and unconstrained coefficient signs without establishing a change to the implemented algorithm.

E1.justification: The evaluated natural and biomedical datasets, ImageNet distribution shifts, and ImageNet-Segmentation task are retained. The alternative backbone and segmentation experiments already appear in v1's appendices; the new semantic analyses examine existing corpus and head descriptions.

E2.justification: Biomedical few-shot Table 3 adds GDA, ProKeR, XCoOp, DCPL, and CLIP-LoRA across all five shot settings. This substantially expands that comparison, even though several methods already participated in other experiments in v1.

E3.justification: Table 2 adds a rank-1 CLIP-LoRA configuration as a comparable-parameter-budget control alongside the retained rank-2 results. Appendix G introduces a relevance-scoring protocol using GPT-5, Qwen3, and Gemini 3. Existing dataset splits, training schedules, classification metrics, and backbone settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 substantially extends validation of interpretability through human annotation of the biomedical corpus and three-LLM relevance assessment of selected attention-head descriptions. It also adds the parameter-budget control and explicit SVD preprocessing profiling. The earlier component, layer, modality, rank, saliency, and t-SNE analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report classification means from three independent runs/support sets. The new relevance evaluation also reports averages only; v3 adds no dispersion estimates, confidence intervals, significance tests, or documented increase in classification runs.

E6.justification: Substantial new results accompany the expanded comparisons and analyses. Examples include rank-1 CLIP-LoRA accuracies of 72.16% and 82.83% at 1 and 16 shots, mean semantic relevance of 3.97, and preprocessing times of 12.16 seconds for CLIP and 15.23 seconds for BiomedCLIP. Matched existing benchmark scores, including the detailed per-dataset appendix tables, remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(15), the SVD formulation, and the TextSpan subspace argument are retained. Added sign-handling explanations and parameter-count breakdowns clarify the existing implementation without introducing substantive new theoretical results, assumptions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and first contribution shift the central novelty claim from proposing a novel SVD-based adaptation framework to providing the first extensive empirical evaluation of existing SVF in vision-language models. The performance, interpretability, and biomedical-corpus contributions remain.

C2.justification: The former short Limitations section becomes a substantial Discussion addressing LoRA intruder dimensions, preservation of pretrained geometry, restricted expressivity, and why fixed subspaces suit few-shot adaptation. v3 also interprets biomedical comparator weaknesses and the new semantic validation, while retaining the need for broader expert validation.

D1.justification: v3 documents pretrained encoder sources, comparator initialization, cached SVD decomposition, forward-pass reconstruction, sign handling, and detailed parameter counts and preprocessing costs. It explicitly states that the biomedical corpus is released alongside the already advertised code. Existing hyperparameter tables and hardware disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: v3 explicitly positions CLIP-SVD as an application and empirical evaluation of Sun et al.'s SVF, materially revising its novelty positioning. It adds LoRA learning/forgetting literature and LLM-as-judge references to support the expanded discussion and validation.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, contribution wording, and selected explanations are revised; Limitations becomes Discussion and a corpus-statistics appendix is inserted. Most existing prose and the overall method-to-experiments organization remain closely matched.

P2.justification: The document undergoes extensive visual reformatting, including typography, margins, headings, author layout, and float placement. Tables 2–3 expand, and v3 adds the corpus-distribution figure and relevance, parameter-count, and preprocessing tables. Earlier scientific figures are retained and resized or relocated.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens comparison fairness, clarifies attribution to existing SVF, and improves implementation and preprocessing-cost transparency. Corpus review and relevance ratings provide useful additional support, but validation remains limited: judge agreement and uncertainty are absent, and Table S9 labels the scale 0–5 while the text specifies 1–5. These are meaningful, bounded gains rather than a substantial improvement in the paper's established empirical conclusions.
